kept.title: Remote Code Execution via eval()
kept.description: The application uses the dangerous `eval()` function to parse user-provided input in the contributions update flow in `app/routes/contributions.js`.
steps_to_exploit: Log in as a user.
Navigate to the Contributions page.
Enter a malicious payload like `process.exit()` or `require('fs').readdirSync('.')` into the contribution fields (e.g., 'preTax').
Submit the form to execute the payload on the server.
kept.impact: Full system compromise; an attacker can execute arbitrary OS commands, read/delete files, or shut down the server.

evidence.quote: const preTax = eval(req.body.preTax); const afterTax = eval(req.body.afterTax); const roth = eval(req.body.roth);

kept.title: NoSQL Injection via $where operator
kept.description: The `getByUserIdAndThreshold` function in `app/data/allocations-dao.js` uses string concatenation to build a MongoDB `$where` query with unsanitized user input.
steps_to_exploit: Log in as a user.
Navigate to the Allocations page.
Set the 'threshold' filter to a malicious value like `5'; while(true){}; '`.
Submit the request to trigger the infinite loop, causing a Denial of Service.
kept.impact: Denial of Service; data exfiltration of all user records by bypassing filters.

kept.title: Broken Access Control (Insecure DOR)
kept.description: The `/allocations/:userId` route in `app/routes/allocations.js` takes the user ID directly from the URL parameter instead of the secure session object.
steps_to_exploit: Log in as a user (e.g., user1).
Observe the URL for allocations is `/allocations/2`.
Change the URL to `/allocations/1` (admin user) or `/allocations/3`.
View private allocation data belonging to another user.
kept.impact: Unauthorized access to private financial data of other users.

kept.title: Missing Function Level Access Control
kept.description: The benefits routes in `app/routes/index.js` do not enforce the `isAdmin` middleware, allowing any authenticated user to access administrative functions.
steps_to_exploit: Log in as a standard non-admin user.
Manually navigate to `/benefits`.
Note that the user is not redirected and can see or update employee benefits.
kept.impact: Unauthorized modification of sensitive employee data; elevation of privilege.

evidence.quote: app.get("/benefits", isLoggedIn, benefitsHandler.displayBenefits); app.post("/benefits", isLoggedIn, benefitsHandler.updateBenefits);

kept.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
kept.description: The `ResearchHandler` in `app/routes/research.js` accepts user-supplied URL and symbol parameters to fetch content from the server.
steps_to_exploit: Access the `/research` page.
Intercept the request and modify the `url` parameter to point to an internal-only service (e.g., `http://127.0.0.1:27017` or cloud metadata services like `http://169.254.169.254/`).
View the response to exfiltrate internal system information.
kept.impact: Exfiltration of internal network resources, service enumeration, or cloud metadata theft.

kept.title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
kept.description: The application disables auto-escaping in the template engine and stores unsanitized input in the database.
steps_to_exploit: Log in as a user.
Go to the Profile or Memos section.
Inject a payload like `<script>alert(document.cookie)</script>` in an input field.
View the page where the content is rendered.
kept.impact: Session hijacking, credential theft, and unauthorized actions performed on behalf of users.

kept.title: Unvalidated Redirects
kept.description: The `/learn` route in `app/routes/index.js` uses a user-supplied query string to redirect users without validation.
steps_to_exploit: Construct a URL: `/learn?url=http://malicious-site.com`.
Send this link to a victim.
Victim clicks the link, thinking it is part of the trusted application.
kept.impact: Phishing and delivery of malware to users via trusted domains.

evidence.quote: app.get("/learn", isLoggedIn, (req, res) => { // Insecure way to handle redirects by taking redirect url from query string return res.redirect(req.query.url); });

kept.title: Broken Authentication: Weak Password Storage
kept.description: User passwords are stored in plain text in the database in `app/data/user-dao.js`.
steps_to_exploit: Gain access to the database (e.g., via SQLi or physical theft).
Read the users collection.
See the plain text passwords.
kept.impact: Total compromise of user accounts if the database is exposed.

kept.title: Sensitive Data Exposure (Insecure Session Management)
kept.description: Session cookies are missing the `httpOnly` and `secure` flags, and the session secret is hardcoded in `config/env/all.js`.
steps_to_exploit: Perform a Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attack to capture session cookies.
Use the captured session ID to impersonate the user.
Access the application without credentials.
kept.impact: Session hijacking and unauthorized access to user accounts.

evidence.quote: app.use(session({ secret: cookieSecret, saveUninitialized: true, resave: true }));

kept.title: Exposure of Debugging Information
kept.description: The application prints the entire configuration object (including potential keys) to the console in `config/config.js`.
steps_to_exploit: Access the server logs (standard output).
Read the printed configuration object.
kept.impact: Leakage of sensitive server-side configuration, including secrets and API keys.

kept.title: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
kept.description: The application does not enforce CSRF protection on critical state-changing forms (e.g., contributions, profile updates).
steps_to_exploit: Create a malicious form that submits data to `/contributions`.
Host the form on an attacker-controlled site.
Trick a logged-in user into visiting the site and submitting the form.
kept.impact: Unauthorized modification of user settings or state.

kept.title: Insecure Database Connection Configuration
kept.description: The database connection string in `config/env/all.js` defaults to `localhost` without requiring authentication.
steps_to_exploit: Gain access to the local network or the host machine.
Connect to the MongoDB instance without credentials to read or modify data.
kept.impact: Full database access; data loss or manipulation.

kept.title: Verbose Error Messages
kept.description: The `error-template.html` reflects raw error objects back to the user, potentially exposing stack traces and internal logic.
steps_to_exploit: Trigger an application error (e.g., by sending malformed input to a controller).
The error page renders the raw `err` object, revealing system paths or code structure.
kept.impact: Information disclosure useful for further attacks.
